name: Sandbox0

modes.label: Sandbox0 Cloud, memory-only meter (CPU included)
modes.note: $0.015 per GiB-hour of the configured memory limit (~$0.000004167/GiB-s), billed per second, no 1-hour minimum; there is no CPU line. CPU is 'platform-derived from memory' and not user-settable; the ratio is unpublished. ram_per_vcpu [2,null] is inferred from the vendor's own comparison row (2 vCPU / 4 GiB) and the ComputeSDK DAX host view (8 CPUs / 16 GiB), not a documented rule. Paused = compute stops; filesystem-only by default. Funded by top-ups: running sandboxes are auto-paused once unpaid usage reaches 10% of the last top-up. [basis verified 2026-09-28] Allocation confirmed: "billed by the second using the configured memory limit"; "No separate CPU charge; CPU limits still apply"; "Paused sandboxes stop compute charges" (sandbox0.ai/pricing). Auto-pause: "ttl | Soft runtime timeout. Expiry requests the same planned pause transaction" (docs/sandbox/pause-resume.md) - docs describe it as pause after idle time; exact idle definition unstated.

modes.label: Managed Agents (Sandpi Platform): sandbox runtime free, pay model tokens + 5% top-up fee
modes.commit_note: Prepaid credit required to create/fork Environments and submit Runs; a 5% fee applies to every credit top-up.
modes.note: Different product: hosted coding-agent runs (Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Kimi Code, ZCode). 'No additional Platform sandbox charge'; you pay model tokens at official provider rates plus a 5% fee on credit top-ups. Only applies when the workload is agent runs on their harness, not raw sandboxes. Sandbox sizes/limits on this platform unpublished; the $0 sandbox cost here excludes LLM token spend, which the engine does not model.

evidence.quote: Use `allow-all` or `block-all` as the unmatched-traffic default.
Cloud metadata and host credential endpoints are protected by the platform. An `allow-all` policy or explicit allow rule cannot grant access to those destinations.
No. Ingress is free, egress is temporarily free, and object-store GET and PUT requests have no per-request charge.

plans.name: Pay as you go (prepaid top-ups)
plans.note: No plan fee, no published free credit. Default team quotas: 20 running sandboxes (paused ones don't count), 5 claims/s, 100 API req/s (burst 200). Quota increases are free on request (contact@sandbox0.ai), subject to approval. Top-up minimum unpublished.

perf_source: ComputeSDK sandboxes benchmarks: cold_start_tti median 786.68 ms (run 2026-08-07), burst_tti median 14,932.74 ms at 100 concurrent (2026-09-25, p99 27.96 s), DAX total 128.37 s (2026-09-25, host view 8 CPUs / 16 GiB x86_64). No hpc CPU run.
caveats: CPU is not billed and not user-settable: it is derived from the memory limit by an unpublished ratio. ram_per_vcpu [2,null] is inferred (vendor comparison row 2 vCPU/4 GiB, DAX host view 8 CPU/16 GiB); if the real ratio gives fewer vCPU per GiB, a CPU-hungry workload needs more memory and costs more.
Egress is free 'for now' (explicitly temporary); ingress and object-store GET/PUT free.

Persistent rootfs and rootfs snapshots are billed as byte-time at $0.02/GiB-month prorated hourly over 730 h, whether the sandbox is running or paused. Default rootfs size 8 GiB (300 MiB-1 TiB); whether billing is on provisioned size or bytes written is not stated (engine uses workload disk/snapshot GiB). Experimental memory-pause checkpoints: storage billing not documented.
Default quota 20 running sandboxes per team; increases free on request but subject to approval.
Top-up funded: running sandboxes auto-pause (filesystem-only, processes lost) when unpaid usage reaches 10% of the last top-up.
Burst start at 100 concurrent is slow (median ~14.9 s, ComputeSDK score 0) although single cold start is ~0.8 s.
Self-hosting: Apache-2.0 core on your own Nomad + PostgreSQL + S3, no licence fee published and no paid support/enterprise tier found; cost = your own infra (not modelled).
Managed Agents (Sandpi Platform) mode excludes LLM token spend and the 5% top-up fee, which the engine does not model.
Regions not published (docs examples use aws-us-east-1); no GPUs, no public IPv4, no free tier or credits found.

vCPU derivation re-checked 2026-09-28: template docs say "CPU is platform-derived from memory and is intentionally absent from the public API" (ratio unpublished); the vendor's own comparison table on sandbox0.ai/pricing lists Sandbox0 allocation as "2 vCPU / 4 GiB" at $10.95 per GiB-month, which supports ram_per_vcpu [2,null] (a 4 vCPU request is billed as 8 GiB). Compute shows $0 because the only meter is memory; the whole bill is in the memory line.

fleet.tiers: PAYG 20 running sandboxes/team; free-to-request increases subject to approval, ordinary usage fees still apply.
fleet.notes: Paused sandboxes do not count toward running limit. Creation/request and retained template/volume quotas additional; 50/300/1,000 need reviewed increase, not an automatically approved form. No timing/verification checklist published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: `ttl` | Soft runtime timeout. Expiry requests the same planned pause transaction.
snapshot_auto.note: Pause (explicit, ttl idle/soft timeout, or billing pause) publishes the block-COW rootfs head as a checkpoint to object storage and resume (explicit or auto_resume on inbound API/SSH/public route) restores it: 'By default, pause publishes the writable block-COW RootFS head and retires the current runtime allocation.' Automatic paths are filesystem-only: 'Existing calls, TTL pause, and automatic resume keep their filesystem-only behavior.' Memory/processes not included unless you explicitly pause with memory:true (experimental).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: create named rootfs snapshots from a running or paused sandbox
snapshot_on_demand.note: Named rootfs snapshots are filesystem-only ('A named RootFS snapshot still contains filesystem state only'); new sandboxes can be claimed from them ('claim a new sandbox with a named rootfs snapshot'), restore in place on a paused sandbox, and fork running/paused sandboxes. Experimental memory:true pause and memory fork retain processes/memory (on supporting deployments).

harness_api.quote: Sandpi Platform runs coding-agent harnesses in persistent Sandbox0 Environments. You integrate tasks, Sessions, events, files, and usage through an API. Sandpi manages harness execution and the underlying sandbox lifecycle.
harness_api.note: Harnesses: Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Kimi Code, ZCode. Sessions keep native conversation history across Runs (follow-ups), stream/replay Run events, stop a Run, roll back latest Run, fork Environments. Delivered as a sister product 'Sandpi Platform' (api.sandpi.ai, own API token, prepaid credit + 5% top-up fee, sandbox free) - not part of the raw Sandbox0 sandbox API; Sandbox0 itself only offers generic contexts/supervised sessions.

egress_allowlist.quote: `mode` | Default fallback for unmatched traffic: `allow-all` or `block-all`
egress_allowlist.note: Ordered allow/deny trafficRules match domains, CIDRs, ports and classified appProtocols; enforced by the node-side ctld network runtime; updatable at runtime via PUT /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/network. Optional customer-managed SOCKS5 egress proxy.

egress_http_rules.quote: HTTP protocol rules inspect outbound HTTP requests. `httpMatch` scopes the rule to matching requests, while `http` defines the operation policy.
egress_http_rules.note: Methods and paths allow/deny (HTTPS requires tlsMode: terminate-reoriginate, i.e. MITM CA injected into sandbox); also MCP tool-name allow/deny for remote MCP calls; audit mode.

ingress_rules.quote: `auth` | Applies bearer or header authentication before the request reaches the sandbox
ingress_rules.note: Only declared Sandbox Services ports are exposed (ingress.public), with per-route method filter, bearer/header auth, CORS, rate limit; plus Private Previews (authenticated, expiring one-time-bootstrap URLs for loopback-only servers). No IP allowlist found.

secret_proxy.quote: Credential features let Sandbox0 authenticate outbound traffic without placing raw secret material inside the sandbox process.
secret_proxy.note: Team-scoped credential sources + bindings + destination-scoped credentialRules; projections: http_headers, placeholder_substitution (headers/query/body), tls_client_certificate, username_password (SOCKS5/MQTT), ssh_proxy (git-over-SSH: 'The upstream private key is never written into the sandbox'). Rule protocols: http, https, grpc, tls, ssh, socks5, mqtt, redis. HTTPS needs terminate-reoriginate MITM.

volume_attach.quote: The public spec is runtime-neutral: it contains an image, default memory and RootFS storage, guest security class, claim-lifetime ephemeral mounts, environment variables, metadata, and a default network policy.
volume_attach.note: Storage model is a single persistent block-COW rootfs (300 MiB-1 TiB) plus non-persistent ephemeralMounts; no attachable persistent volume object in the docs.

volume_shared.quote: Fork creates a new sandbox with Copy-on-Write rootfs isolation from the source rootfs state.
volume_shared.note: State is shared between sandboxes only by snapshot/fork (CoW copies), not a concurrently mounted shared filesystem; no shared volume documented.

anti_bot.quote: Sandbox0 is an enterprise-grade AI Agent Sandbox platform that enables you to run code securely in isolated environments with full process control
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandbox0 is a generic gVisor code/agent sandbox with no browser or scraping-specific product; no fingerprint-spoofing/stealth feature is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or use-case pages (a Steel Browser use-case shows you can self-install one, not that Sandbox0 provides anti-bot tooling).

captcha_solving.quote: Sandbox0 is an enterprise-grade AI Agent Sandbox platform that enables you to run code securely in isolated environments with full process control
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandbox0 sells raw compute/execution sandboxes, not a browser/scraping product; no CAPTCHA-solving API or feature is documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: Each provider/region (e.g., `aws-us-east-1`) has an independent data plane and control plane deployment with dedicated PostgreSQL and S3 storage.
egress_ip_type.note: Sandboxes run on dedicated Nomad nodes in AWS-hosted regions; outbound traffic leaves from ordinary cloud/datacenter egress paths shared across sandboxes. No residential/mobile IP product is offered; the only IP customization is bringing your own SOCKS5 proxy (see static_egress_ip).

live_resize.quote: A standalone `config.resources.memory` update replaces an existing sandbox's runtime lease, preserving its ID and files while restarting processes.
live_resize.note: CPU is derived from memory, so this also changes effective CPU. The sandbox's identity/ID and files are preserved without recreating it, but the update restarts processes inside it (not a fully seamless resize).

own_agent_api.quote: Sandpi Platform runs coding-agent harnesses in persistent Sandbox0 Environments. You integrate tasks, Sessions, events, files, and usage through an API. Sandpi manages harness execution and the underlying sandbox lifecycle.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Sandbox0's own first-party API drives generic sandboxes (contexts/sessions/files); its harness API (Sandpi/Managed Agents) drives third-party coding harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Kimi Code, ZCode) you choose — there is no Sandbox0-branded browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: Sandbox0 supports HTTP request controls and remote MCP controls over HTTP or HTTPS.
mcp_server.note: This is an egress policy feature that inspects/filters MCP tool calls a sandbox makes outward — not a Sandbox0-shipped MCP server for controlling sandboxes from an MCP client. No MCP server package is listed among the official SDKs (Go/JS/Python) or CLI/GitHub repos in llms.txt.

lang_python.quote: REPL configuration (optional for `type=repl`; defaults to Python when omitted) ... alias | string | REPL alias/language (python, bash, node, etc.)
lang_python.note: Python REPL is a built-in context type and is the default when no alias is given; first-party Go/Python/TypeScript SDKs also expose sandbox.run("python", ...).

lang_node.quote: `alias` | string | REPL alias/language (python, bash, node, etc.)
lang_node.note: Node is a documented built-in REPL alias alongside python and bash.

guest_firewall.quote: `securityClass` | No | The only supported value is `privileged`, which is also the default. Capabilities apply inside the gVisor guest and do not bypass runsc or expose host devices.
guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is gVisor (a userspace network-stack sandbox), not a full VM/microVM, so kernel netfilter/nftables is not the real kernel firewall and iptables/nftables inside the guest is not expected to configure genuine packet filtering; not documented as working.

static_egress_ip.quote: Sandbox egress proxy routes allowed outbound TCP traffic through a customer-managed SOCKS5 proxy. Use it when a sandbox needs a customer-controlled egress IP, customer-side audit, or access to services reachable from the proxy network.
static_egress_ip.note: Sandbox0 has no first-party static egress IP; a fixed outbound IP is only achievable by pointing the sandbox's egress at your own (customer-managed) SOCKS5 proxy.

byoc.quote: Sandbox0 self-hosting uses dedicated Nomad client nodes, stock gVisor `runsc`, direct node services, regional PostgreSQL, and S3-compatible RootFS storage.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope as documented. Sandbox0 offers either its own multi-tenant Cloud or fully self-hosted (you operate everything on your own infra); there is no documented managed/BYOC mode where Sandbox0 operates the control plane inside a customer's own cloud account.

soc2.quote: Sandbox0 is AI agent infrastructure with sandbox execution, persistent workspaces, network control, and fast runtime startup.
soc2.note: No security/trust/compliance page exists on the site (/security and /trust both 404) and no SOC 2 mention appears in docs, pricing, blog, or the sitemap; treated as not currently attested.

hipaa.quote: Sandbox0 is AI agent infrastructure with sandbox execution, persistent workspaces, network control, and fast runtime startup.
hipaa.note: No HIPAA/BAA mention found anywhere on the site, docs, or sitemap; no compliance page exists.

sso.quote: Authenticate with `s0 auth login` for interactive CLI use ... create a team-scoped API key and export it as `SANDBOX0_TOKEN`
sso.note: Documented auth is device-code CLI login plus team-scoped API keys; no SAML/OIDC SSO is mentioned anywhere in the docs or pricing pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: Each provider/region (e.g., `aws-us-east-1`) has an independent data plane and control plane deployment with dedicated PostgreSQL and S3 storage.
eu_data_residency.note: The only region named anywhere in the docs is the example `aws-us-east-1`; no region list or EU region is published for Sandbox0 Cloud (self-hosting in the EU is possible but is a separate self-hosted regime, not managed EU data residency).

max_session_h.quote: `ttl` | Soft runtime timeout. Expiry requests the same planned pause transaction. `hard_ttl` | Hard sandbox timeout. Expiry durably requests deletion of identity and RootFS state.
max_session_h.note: ttl/hard_ttl are optional, caller-set timers with no documented platform-imposed maximum; a sandbox with no hard_ttl set keeps its checkpointed identity indefinitely and can be resumed at any time, so there is no fixed max single-session cap analogous to E2B/Daytona style hour limits.

nested_virt.quote: The privileged class grants capabilities only inside the gVisor guest.
nested_virt.note: Isolation is gVisor (runsc) per self-hosted.md ('stock gVisor runsc'); Docker-in-Sandbox runs Docker inside the gVisor guest via a 'privileged' security class, not a KVM/hardware-virt device. No /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability documented anywhere in the docs, template configuration, or self-hosted install guides.

desktop.quote: The template includes Chromium, Playwright CLI, TigerVNC, Openbox, and a WebSocket bridge dependency. These are installed at build time; claiming a sandbox does not start a desktop or download a browser. Applications such as Sandpi start the desktop on demand and expose an authenticated viewer.
desktop.note: The built-in coding-agent template ships a full graphical desktop stack (TigerVNC VNC server + Openbox window manager + headed Chromium); a Sandbox Service can start it on demand and expose it through the platform's ingress/viewer path (as documented end-to-end in the Sandpi blog post). It is not started automatically and is not a turnkey 'one field' feature, but the desktop capability itself is a documented first-party building block, not absent, so the recorded 'no' is wrong.

browser.quote: The builtin `browser` template uses the upstream Steel Browser image. It stores Chrome profile data under `/browser/profile` and downloads under `/files` on the sandbox writable rootfs. ... Steel returns `websocketUrl` from `/v1/sessions` ... `debugUrl`, `sessionViewerUrl`
browser.note: Sandbox0 ships a first-party 'browser' template (Steel Browser + Chromium) with CDP, live/debug view, profile persistence, and public ingress managed by the platform itself ('Platform administrators manage a public browser template through the normal template API'). This directly satisfies 'a real browser available/managed', so the recorded 'no' is wrong.

computer_use.quote: VNC carries pixels, keyboard input, and pointer input for the human. CDP lets the agent inspect and automate pages. ... This is why Sandbox0 does not need a universal browser API.
computer_use.note: Agent-facing automation is CDP/Playwright (browser_control), and the desktop/VNC path is for a human viewer, not an agent screenshot+click API. No screenshot-plus-click 'computer use' endpoint is documented anywhere in the docs.

volumes.quote: The public spec is runtime-neutral: it contains an image, default memory and RootFS storage, guest security class, claim-lifetime ephemeral mounts, environment variables, metadata, and a default network policy.
volumes.note: Storage model is a single persistent block-COW rootfs (300 MiB-1 TiB) plus non-persistent claim-lifetime ephemeralMounts; there is no attachable/detachable extra persistent volume object anywhere in the docs (matches the card's own volume_attach/volume_shared evidence).

public_ipv4.quote: Sandbox0 terminates SSH at a region-scoped `ssh-gateway`, authenticates the user from uploaded SSH public keys, and bridges the session into the sandbox runtime.
public_ipv4.note: SSH is reached through a shared regional gateway host (not a per-sandbox IP), and public HTTP services are reached via subdomain routing (`https://<sandbox_id>--p<port>.<region_id>.<root_domain>` per services.md), not a public IPv4 address. No public IPv4 offering is documented.

agent_harnesses.quote: The `Update Coding Agent Template` workflow refreshes the npm `latest` stable versions of Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, and Playwright CLI every three UTC days.
agent_harnesses.note: The built-in `coding-agent` template preinstalls Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi as coding-agent harnesses (kept up to date by an automated workflow), directly matching the field definition. The card's own managed-agents mode already lists agent_harnesses: true; the top-level/on-demand 'false' is inconsistent and wrong.

gpu.quote: Compute is billed by the second using the configured memory limit. The GiB-hour rate is an equivalent price. ... Persistent rootfs data is measured as byte-time.
gpu.note: Pricing lists only a single memory-based compute meter plus storage/network; no GPU line, GPU pricing, or GPU instance type appears anywhere on the pricing page, in self-hosted infra docs (dedicated Nomad clients, gVisor runsc), or in the template/configuration spec.

windows.quote: Sandbox0 self-hosting uses dedicated Nomad client nodes, stock gVisor runsc, direct node services, regional PostgreSQL, and S3-compatible RootFS storage.
windows.note: Sandbox0 is a gVisor (runsc) Linux-container sandbox platform; every template, image, and runtime-class doc is Linux/OCI-image based. Windows machines are outside the product's scope (Windows only appears as a client OS for installing the `s0` CLI).

macos.quote: Sandbox0 self-hosting uses dedicated Nomad client nodes, stock gVisor runsc, direct node services, regional PostgreSQL, and S3-compatible RootFS storage.
macos.note: Same as windows: the sandbox runtime is Linux/gVisor-only; macOS only appears as a client OS for the `s0` CLI installer, not as a sandbox machine type. Outside the product's scope.

arm64.quote: Until the public API exposes an explicit class selector, configure exactly one compatible class for each requested cluster. Zero or multiple matches fail
arm64.note: Compatibility classes include 'CPU architecture and RootFS artifact platform', but Sandbox0 Cloud currently exposes no public architecture selector (one class per cluster) and the only observed host platform (ComputeSDK benchmark) is x86_64. Multi-arch (amd64+arm64) image builds are a CI detail of the coding-agent template's own container image, not an offered arm64 sandbox runtime for customers.

cpu_class.quote: enough free CPU and memory in the dedicated node cpuset ... a claim also requires ... the production acceptance gate requires at least eight ready carriers, eight truthful dedicated CPU cores, enough non-oversubscribed memory
cpu_class.note: CPU is derived from the memory allocation by an unpublished ratio and is not directly priced, but the docs are explicit that CPU is leased as an exact, non-oversubscribed cpuset carved out of dedicated node capacity ('Manager leases exact CPU and memory from ctld-reported dedicated-node capacity'; self-hosted.md: 'Manager and PostgreSQL atomically lease exact sandbox CPU and memory from ctld-advertised node capacity'), which matches 'dedicated' rather than shared/burstable vCPUs. Managed Agents (Sandpi) runs coding-agent harnesses inside the same underlying Sandbox0 sandbox runtime, so the same dedicated-cpuset allocation model applies, though Sandpi's own sandbox sizing/limits are otherwise unpublished (medium confidence for that mode).
